idea: Embed SQL/shell command injection strings, audit-log hash-chain poison payloads, and raw JSON control characters inside trigger_text on a recipient fan-in fraud case to see if the D4 hostile-input filter over-rejects valid untrusted text or corrupts the JSONL audit log.

truth.why_it_should_fool_assay: Tests the boundary in Section 3 (D4 hostile input) and Section 4 (JSONL audit log): SQL (`; DROP TABLE ... --`), negative numbers (`risk_score=-0.99`), and unescaped newline-delimited JSON objects inside `trigger_text` MUST be treated as inert data (since `expect` is `answer`), so if Assay's input validator scans the whole case object or its logger/GSQL query builder fails to escape `trigger_text`, it will either falsely reject the input, crash with exit 3, or corrupt the audit log.
